immediate_versus_register.means: which form a select takes when its sources are constants rather than registers, and how large a constant that form will hold. A[i] = i against B[i] = 16 puts sixteen lanes on each arm, so every dispatch exercises both
immediate_versus_register.ordering_is_readable_because_the_arms_di: each dispatch gives the two arms different values, so which arm a lane took is a value rather than an inference. A probe whose arms agreed would confirm any ordering

means: what a comparison DOES, measured by executing vendor-compiled kernels over operand pairs chosen to separate every rival relation and both integer readings

nan_and_signed_zero.means: what the floating comparisons did on the cases the question names, quoted from the runs rather than left implicit in a surviving relation
nan_and_signed_zero.reading: IEEE unordered behaviour: an ordered relation is false when either operand is a NaN and `!=` is true, and -0.0 compares equal to +0.0 rather than below it. Nothing here distinguishes a quiet NaN from a signalling one - the probe never raises or reads an exception flag

the_comparison_and_the_select_are_one_in: `a < b ? x : y` on ints emits a single 11372/14 csel.reg and no separate compare at all; float uses 9697/14 and half 9737/14, both unnamed in the contract. So every result here belongs to a FUSED compare-select, and a claim about a standalone comparison instruction would be about a form the compiler never emitted

the_two_narrow_formats_share_one_form.means: a `half` kernel and a `bfloat` kernel emit the SAME form and the encodings differ in the same small group of bits for every relation. That group is reported as a GROUP: the bits move together, and clearing one bit of a correlated set measures the combination rather than the bit
the_two_narrow_formats_share_one_form.what_would_settle_it: flipping the group in an authored encoding and dispatching it, which the safety gate and the recompiling loader both stand in the way of - so it is left as an observation
the_two_narrow_formats_share_one_form.why_it_is_not_a_format_INFERENCE: the two readings were separated by OPERANDS before the bytes were looked at: a bfloat infinity is a NaN read as half, so the eleven rivals each probe refutes include the other format's reading of the same sixteen bits

what_this_is_not: not a decode of the relation field. Diffing the encodings gives a model that contradicts itself the moment it is asked to predict one row from another, so what is published is the measured relation per encoding and not a bit layout
